pi: Block the proteasome, the cell's machinery for clearing unwanted proteins, so misfolded proteins build up and trigger cell death. Myeloma cells, which make large amounts of immunoglobulin, are especially sensitive; in mantle cell lymphoma, bortezomib also suppresses NF-κB survival signalling. Bortezomib binds reversibly, carfilzomib irreversibly; ixazomib is taken by mouth.
imid: Bind cereblon and redirect its ubiquitin ligase to destroy the transcription factors Ikaros and Aiolos, which kills myeloma cells and activates T and NK cells. Lenalidomide and pomalidomide are IMiDs; the newer CELMoDs (iberdomide, mezigdomide) bind cereblon more tightly and degrade the targets faster and more completely, so they keep activity in IMiD-refractory disease.
cd38: Monoclonal antibodies against CD38, which is highly expressed on myeloma cells. They kill through complement, antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and phagocytosis, and also deplete CD38-positive immunosuppressive cells. Daratumumab and isatuximab.
hdac: Panobinostat inhibits histone deacetylases, including HDAC6, which myeloma cells use to clear misfolded protein through the aggresome when the proteasome is blocked. That is the rationale for pairing it with bortezomib.
slamf7: Elotuzumab binds SLAMF7 on myeloma cells and NK cells, activating NK cells directly and marking myeloma cells for antibody-dependent killing. It has little activity alone and is given with an IMiD.
xpo1: Selinexor blocks exportin 1 (XPO1), the protein that moves tumor suppressors such as p53 out of the nucleus. Trapping them in the nucleus, and lowering oncoprotein levels, leads to cell death.
bcl2: Venetoclax inhibits BCL2, a protein that keeps cells from dying. Myeloma with t(11;14) is often dependent on BCL2, which is why the benefit concentrates in that subgroup.
bela: An antibody-drug conjugate: an antibody against BCMA carries the microtubule toxin MMAF into myeloma cells. The payload also causes the corneal toxicity typical of the drug.
melflufen: A lipophilic peptide conjugate of an alkylating agent that enters cells readily and is cleaved by aminopeptidases, which myeloma cells overexpress, releasing melphalan inside the cell.
cart: The patient's own T cells are engineered to carry a chimeric antigen receptor against BCMA; after a single infusion they expand and kill BCMA-expressing myeloma cells. Idecabtagene vicleucel and ciltacabtagene autoleucel.
tce: Bispecific antibodies bind CD3 on T cells with one arm and a myeloma antigen with the other, bringing the patient's T cells into contact with tumor cells without manufacturing a cell product. Teclistamab, elranatamab and linvoseltamab target BCMA; talquetamab targets GPRC5D.
gprc5d: GPRC5D is a receptor on myeloma cells that is independent of BCMA, so it remains a target after BCMA-directed therapy. It is also expressed in keratinized tissues, which explains the skin, nail and taste toxicity of talquetamab.
bcl2L: BCL2 is a protein that keeps cells from dying, and mantle cell lymphoma and many other B-cell lymphomas depend on it. Venetoclax and the newer, more selective sonrotoclax block it, releasing the cell's own death program. BCL2 inhibition complements BTK inhibition, which is the rationale for combining them.
benda: An alkylating agent with a purine-like ring, which may explain its activity in lymphomas resistant to other alkylators. It damages DNA and causes prolonged lymphocyte depletion, which contributes to its infection risk.
btk: BTK carries the B-cell receptor's survival signal, on which mantle cell lymphoma and other B-cell lymphomas depend. Covalent inhibitors (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib) bind cysteine 481 permanently, and mutations there cause resistance; noncovalent pirtobrutinib binds reversibly and works despite them. The newer agents are more selective, with less atrial fibrillation and bleeding than ibrutinib.
cd19car: The patient's own T cells are engineered to recognize CD19, present on almost all B-cell lymphomas, and given as a single infusion after lymphodepleting chemotherapy. Brexucabtagene autoleucel, axicabtagene ciloleucel, tisagenlecleucel and lisocabtagene maraleucel differ in their costimulatory domain (CD28 or 4-1BB) and manufacturing, which affects how fast they act and their rates of cytokine release syndrome and neurotoxicity.
cd20: Monoclonal antibodies against CD20, present on nearly all B cells and B-cell lymphomas. Rituximab kills mainly through complement and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity; obinutuzumab, a glycoengineered type II antibody, relies more on direct cell death and cellular cytotoxicity and causes deeper B-cell depletion.
cd20tce: Bispecific antibodies that bind CD20 on lymphoma cells and CD3 on T cells, bringing the patient's own T cells to the tumor without manufacturing a cell product. Mosunetuzumab, glofitamab, epcoritamab and odronextamab; step-up dosing in the first cycles limits cytokine release syndrome.
imidL: In lymphoma, lenalidomide works through cereblon, degrading the transcription factors Ikaros and Aiolos, and strongly enhances T-cell and NK-cell activity, which is why it pairs well with antibodies (lenalidomide-rituximab) and bispecific antibodies. CELMoDs such as golcadomide are more potent cereblon modulators now in lymphoma trials.
mtor: Temsirolimus inhibits mTOR, a kinase that controls cell growth and protein synthesis, including production of cyclin D1, the protein overexpressed in mantle cell lymphoma through t(11;14).
il6: IL-6 from the bone marrow environment is a growth and survival signal for myeloma cells. Siltuximab is an antibody that neutralizes IL-6; in smoldering myeloma its randomized trial did not meet its primary endpoint.
rit: An anti-CD20 antibody carrying a radioactive isotope (yttrium-90 in ibritumomab tiuxetan), so radiation reaches the targeted cells and neighbouring lymphoma cells as well. Lymphoma is very radiosensitive; the main toxicity is delayed, prolonged cytopenias.
cd19ab: Tafasitamab is an Fc-engineered antibody against CD19, built to enhance antibody-dependent killing by NK cells and macrophages. Lenalidomide boosts NK-cell activity, which is the rationale for pairing them.
ezh2: EZH2 is an enzyme that silences genes by methylating histones; activating EZH2 mutations, found in about a fifth of follicular lymphomas, lock B cells in a germinal-center state. Tazemetostat inhibits EZH2 and is active in both mutant and wild-type disease, more often with the mutation.
pi3k: PI3K, especially its delta form in B cells, carries survival signals from the B-cell receptor. Idelalisib, copanlisib, duvelisib and umbralisib block it, but immune-mediated toxicity (colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis), infections and a survival concern in related trials led to the loss of every US follicular lymphoma indication.
